note: Attacker-controlled constructor argument supplies the attribute name string.
The name is validated; a non-zero result would reject the input, so a valid name continues into object creation.
A new libxml attribute node is allocated from the attacker-controlled name/value.
The DOMAttr object may already wrap a previous libxml node, which is fetched before replacement.

If an old node exists, it is freed before the new node is installed; the vulnerability hypothesis is that this path can free uninitialized or otherwise invalid memory when the wrapper has not been properly initialized.
The new node pointer replaces the wrapper state after the free, so any invalid free occurs at the sink immediately before reassignment.
